title: POC weekly sync - model selection & pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing model selection and pinning strategy. Reviewed latest benchmark results (latency, token cost, hallucination rates), discussed fallback and rollback plans, and agreed next steps: run 24h stability test on dedicated nodes, pin traffic to rwd-3b-quant-v2 for low-latency paths with fallback to rwd-7b-heap if quality regresses, and Redwood to share security + pricing docs.
action_items: Ben Cho (Redwood SE): run 24h stability perf run on dedicated c4 nodes, attach logs and csv metrics > due 2026-12-29
Alice Martinez (Redwood AE): send updated pricing worksheet and sample contract language > due 2026-12-24
Rachel Lin (Maple): share 3 canonical prompt sets and failure cases observed in prod > due 2026-12-24
Samir Patel (Maple): provide VPC / peering details and expected throughput for pilot > due 2026-12-28
next_steps: Redwood to run stability and inversion tests and share raw results
Maple to validate rwd-3b-quant-v2 outputs on their regression set
Schedule a 45-min canary rollout planning session week of 2026-12-29
Exchange security docs (SOC2, data residency, KMS integration) and finalize Private deployment checklist
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Rachel Lin (Maple - Head of ML), Samir Patel (Maple - Platform), Jenna Morris (Maple - Product)

Summary: quick review of benchmarks, confirm model pinning for pilot, discuss fallbacks and rollbacks, agree next steps.

[00:00] Alice Martinez: ok hi everyone thanks for joining uh happy holidays early uh we're trying to keep this one short today, agenda is benchmarks, pinning, and rollbacks, ben you wanna kick off with the perf numbers?
[00:18] Ben Cho: yeah sure, thanks alice. so we ran the last two days of runs on the dedicated c4s you asked for, and i have the aggregated numbers here. median latency for rwd-3b-quant-v2 is about 220ms p95 is 480ms at your typical 1-2 token chunk size, cost per 1k tokens is roughly $0.38 on our estimate. the rwd-7b-heap model shows better quality on the hallucination regression set but latency is p95 ~ 1.1s and cost ~ $0.9 per 1k tokens.
[00:46] Rachel Lin: okay those numbers align with what we saw internally, one clarifying q though: the 220ms is warm-cache? cold-start adds how much?
[00:56] Ben Cho: good call - warm-cache numbers, cold is variable, we saw first-token extra of about 120-200ms on first request after idle, but with prefix KV caching for repeated flows it's much less frequent. for the pilot we recommend a keepalive policy to avoid cold starts.
[01:18] Samir Patel: are those dedicated node runs or hosted? we wanna simulate our expected traffic shape, which is small bursts 10-20 rps for short windows.
[01:28] Ben Cho: the runs were on a dedicated pool that mirrors what we'd provision for your committed capacity. i can also run a burst profile with your 10-20 rps to show queueing and batching behavior.
[01:39] Jenna Morris: on quality, the product team cares about hallucination rates on the finance prompts, we sent some examples last week, did we run those through both models?
[01:49] Ben Cho: yes, we ran the canonical finance prompt set Rachel shared. rwd-7b-heap had fewer hallucination flags (approx 6% vs 12% for the 3b quant) on that set. but on token-level ROUGE / factuality heuristics the difference is narrower.
[02:08] Rachel Lin: hmm 6% vs 12% is meaningful for compliance. what about output length variance — we sometimes need more verbose responses. does the 3b quant truncate more?
[02:18] Ben Cho: there was a slight tendency to be terser, likely due to decoding defaults we used (top-p 0.92, temp 0.2). we can tune decode params; that will help with verbosity without changing model.
[02:32] Alice Martinez: this is the core tradeoff we talked about — lat/cost vs small quality gains. for the pilot recommended path: pin majority traffic to rwd-3b-quant-v2 to meet latency SLOs but configure a quality-check routing that can route a fraction to rwd-7b-heap, and keep an automatic rollback/fallback to rwd-7b if we see quality regressions above threshold. thoughts?
[02:58] Rachel Lin: that feels reasonable as long as the fallback triggers are conservative and transparent. we need to know exactly what triggers the fallback — is it a fixed hallucination rate threshold from our regression prompts or something adaptive?
[03:12] Ben Cho: we can do both: start with a static threshold you set (e.g., >8% hallucination on sampled evals over a 30-minute window) and we can add adaptive heuristics later. alerts and traces will show examples.
[03:28] Samir Patel: about routing — can we have region-aware routing? some of our users are in EMEA and we want to route those requests to eu nodes to reduce latency.
[03:36] Alice Martinez: yep, smart routing supports region policy. for the POC we'll pin model versions per route and per region — easy to configure in the console.
[03:45] Jenna Morris: what about canary deploys? we want to roll model changes gradually.
[03:50] Ben Cho: rollout features support canary percentage, A/B tests, and automatic rollback if key metrics degrade. for POC we recommend a 10/90 canary for any model change with automatic rollback on regressed metrics for 2 consecutive evaluation windows.
[04:06] Rachel Lin: ok good. circling back to security: we need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details before we move data to dedicated nodes. any news on that?
[04:16] Alice Martinez: yes, i'll share the security pack after this call — SOC2, encryption at rest details, KMS/HSM integration patterns, audit log examples. we can also provide a redacted SOC2 report under NDA.
[04:28] Samir Patel: and for private deployment — if we decide to do VPC peering, what are the latency implications? we need numbers if we go that route.
[04:36] Ben Cho: typically the extra network hop is small, 10-40ms depending on region and peering. we can run a synthetic test from your VPC to a private node to measure. i'll add that to the perf run.
[04:50] Rachel Lin: one more practical question: if we pin to the quantized 3b and later decide to upgrade the weights to a 3b-v3, how hard is rollback?
[04:58] Ben Cho: model pinning is versioned. you can pin traffic to a specific model-version id; upgrades are atomic and you can stage with canaries. rollback is immediate to previous version; we also support automatic fallback to a different model family if pinned model is unhealthy.
[05:15] Alice Martinez: okay let's walk through an example: we pin 90% traffic to rwd-3b-quant-v2, 10% to rwd-7b-heap for quality checks. threshold for rollback set to 8% hallucination on sampled evals over 30m. Ben will run stability and the 24h burst tests and provide logs. Rachel you'll validate on your regression set and if quality acceptable we move to canary rollout.
[05:39] Jenna Morris: do we need any infra changes on our side? Samir?
[05:43] Samir Patel: we'll need to open peering ports and provide service account details for RW to provision dedicated nodes; also we need to confirm throughput limits with our infra team.
[05:53] Alice Martinez: understood. Ben, can you confirm timelines for the runs?
[05:56] Ben Cho: i can start the 24h stability run today and have a summary by end of day friday, 2026-12-24; the burst profile will be done by monday 2026-12-28 with the detailed CSV exports.
[06:08] Rachel Lin: sounds good. for the pilot success criteria — we'll define it as p95 latency < 600ms for 90% of traffic and hallucination < 8% on regression set and cost per 1k tokens below $0.6.
[06:24] Ben Cho: got it, i'll include those as target thresholds in the run and set alerts on them.
[06:31] Alice Martinez: quick note on cost controls — we can set per-route quotas and token limits, helpful for pilots.
[06:36] Jenna Morris: perfect. any blockers on the security front?
[06:39] Alice Martinez: no blockers, just paperwork — i'll send docs and the link to the security deck.
[06:44] Samir Patel: one last question — are there recommended decode settings for finance prompts? we currently call with top-p 0.95 temp 0.3, do you recommend adjusting?
[06:53] Ben Cho: we saw less hallucination with slightly lower top-p and temp (top-p 0.92 temp 0.2) on the 3b quant; for the 7b you can actually loosen to top-p 0.96 if you need more verbosity. we'll include a recommended decode config per-model in the notes.
[07:06] Rachel Lin: thanks. also please include example traces where fallback would have kicked in so we can review.
[07:12] Ben Cho: will do, i'll include sample traces and request/response payloads in the perf artifacts.
[07:18] Alice Martinez: okay wrapping up — high level next steps and owners...
[07:23] [Section: Recap & next steps]
[07:25] Alice Martinez: Action items: Ben run stability + burst tests; Alice share pricing + security docs; Rachel share canonical prompts and failure cases; Samir share VPC peering details. We'll reconvene after results. thanks everyone and happy holidays.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-heard technical terms (eg. 'heap' occasionally transcribed as 'heat' in one snippet) — SE corrected live.
